subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [Safeway Stores, Inc. v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. of Pittsburgh, Penn., supra, 64 F3d at 1287; Nordstrom, Inc. v. Chubb & Son, Inc. (9th Cir. 1995) 54 F3d 1424, 1432 (applying Wash. law)] (b) [3:712] Other cases allocate settlement costs based on “relative exposure”: Some other decisions allow allocation of settlements according to each defendant's “relative exposure,” making it less likely that the D&O insurer will be responsible for the entire settlement. [Slottow v. American Cas. Co. of Reading, Penn. (9th Cir. 1993) 10 F3d 1355, 1359 (applying Calif. law)] Comment: Subsequent Ninth Circuit decisions have interpreted Slottow's “relative exposure” analysis to apply only where the parties have already agreed to an allocation; i.e., Slottow did not address an insurer's right to allocate in the absence of such agreement.
